descriptionChirho: A gentillic adjective denoting an inhabitant or native of the Aramean territory of Maacah (מַעֲכָה), used to identify specific individuals: Eshtemoa the Maacathite (1 Chronicles 4:19), Jaazaniah the Maacathite (2 Kings 25:23; Jeremiah 40:8), and in broader references to the Maacathite people in the Transjordan region (Deuteronomy 3:14; Joshua 12:5, 13:11, 13:13). All eight occurrences carry the same gentillic meaning. Cross-linguistically: Arabic المَعْكَاتِيّ (al-Ma'kaatiyy), Spanish 'maacateo/maacatita' (using Romance gentillic suffixes), Hindi माकाती (Maakaatii), Korean 마아갓 사람/마아가인 (Maagat saram/Maagain, 'person from Maacah'), Swahili 'Mmaakathi/Wamaakathi' (singular/plural noun class). All three clusters differ only in the presence of the article and/or conjunctive waw, which are grammatical, not semantic.
